statements.impact_statement: GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2 (GitHub and osv.dev list no CVE alias for it) is a cross-site request forgery bypass in React Router's unstable React Server Components (RSC) server mode: when a mutation request failed the origin check, the RSC request handler still ran the route action before returning the 400 response. It affects the npm package react-router from 7.12.0 to before 7.18.2 and from 8.0.0 to before 8.3.0, and the advisory states it only affects applications that use the unstable RSC APIs: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2. The fix, https://github.com/remix-run/react-router/commit/8ebd5df9932854547963e3255c8454e62430e05d in 7.18.2 (https://github.com/remix-run/react-router/commit/7a71c728ad116bd78699a258b2014ce9585729f5 on the main branch), changes only lib/rsc/server.rsc.ts in the library source, where generateRenderResponse now downgrades a request that fails the origin check to a GET so that no action runs; both commits also add a test and a release note. In the react-router 7.16.0, 7.18.0 and 7.18.2 npm packages, generateRenderResponse and the RSC server request handler matchRSCServerRequest are compiled only into the react-server entry point (index-react-server.js and index-react-server.mjs, under dist/development and dist/production; matchRSCServerRequest is otherwise named only in TypeScript declaration files and, in 7.18.0 and 7.18.2, in the bundled documentation page docs/how-to/react-server-components.md). Those two files are also the only ones that carry the strings 'getRequest must be called from within a React Server render context' and 'Cannot handle form actions without a decodeAction function'. Other RSC strings are not limited to that entry point: 'React-Router-Resource' and 'rsc-action-id' also appear in the default entry point (in its RSC server-rendering helper, routeRSCServerRequest), and 'rsc-action-id' and 'text/x-component' in the browser RSC entry point (dom-export). Jaeger serves its web UI as static files: /usr/bin/jaeger embeds the prebuilt browser assets of the jaeger-ui release with the same version number as gzip-compressed files, and there is no Node.js server. We downloaded every jaeger-dev package published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository as of 2026-11-28: 21 builds, 2.19.0-r1 to the current 2.23.0-r4, each for x86_64 and aarch64 (42 packages), each matched to its index entry. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/jaeger, a statically linked Go program for Linux (no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies) built with CGO_ENABLED=0 and GOOS=linux, without -trimpath, as its Go build information records. In every one of those programs we decompressed every gzip stream in /usr/bin/jaeger and searched the JavaScript. The bundle records the React Router version it was built with (window.__reactRouterVersion): 7.16.0 in 2.19.0-r1 to 2.19.0-r4, 7.18.0 in 2.20.0-r0 to 2.20.0-r5, and 7.18.2 from 2.21.0-r0, matching the jaeger-ui lockfiles (https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/blob/v2.19.0/package-lock.json, https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/blob/v2.20.0/pnpm-lock.yaml, https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/blob/v2.21.0/pnpm-lock.yaml). Every bundle contains React Router's browser router (its message 'You cannot render a <Router> inside another <Router>' is found in each, as a control), and none contains either of the two react-server strings above, the name matchRSCServerRequest, or the RSC strings React-Router-Resource, rsc-action-id and text/x-component; a search of the uncompressed binary finds none of them either. So the vulnerable RSC server code is not present in any build, including 2.19.0-r1 to 2.20.0-r5, which bundle an affected React Router version.

The jaeger source package also publishes jaeger-es-index-cleaner, jaeger-es-rollover and their -dev packages, 12 builds each from 2.20.0-5 to the current 2.23.0-4 on amd64 and arm64 (48 packages per architecture). The control-archive MD5 manifest of every one of them lists a single file, the Go program /usr/bin/es-index-cleaner or /usr/bin/es-rollover; these command-line tools embed no web UI. The 2.20.0-5 builds are the only ones from a jaeger release whose UI bundles an affected React Router (7.18.0; from 2.21.0 it is 7.18.2), and we unpacked all eight of them (base and -dev of both tools, on amd64 and arm64). In each program the 13 embedded gzip streams (20,446 bytes in all) are compressed protobuf descriptors, and neither they nor the uncompressed program contain React Router code (no 'You cannot render a <Router> inside another <Router>' message and no __reactRouterVersion) or any of the RSC strings above.
